target_gate: Find one real Egyptian text where cloth/wrapping + oil/liquid + soaking/moistening + wringing/pressing occur in one local instruction or tightly connected procedure.

strongest_single_text_match.source: Papyrus Edwin Smith, 17th Dynasty, case sequence around column 5
strongest_single_text_match.transliteration_primary: wdi̯.ḫr=k sšm.wj.DU n(.j) ḥbs jwḥ m mrḥ.t m-ẖnw msꜣḏ.t.DU=fj
strongest_single_text_match.semantic_summary: Two swabs/plugs made of cloth/linen are specified as moistened with oil/fat and placed into the nostrils; a nearby parallel instruction repeats the same cloth + oil/fat + moistening structure.

modern_to_ancient_projection.modern: PAD -> OIL + WATER -> UPTAKE -> RETRIEVE -> WRING/PRESS -> RECOVER OIL
modern_to_ancient_projection.missing_edge: OIL-BEARING CLOTH -> WRING/PRESS -> RECOVER OIL IN THE SAME PROCEDURE

scientific_boundary: The Edwin Smith passage is a medical treatment using oil-moistened linen swabs. It does not describe SCOBY, oil sorption cleanup, wringing those swabs, or recovering oil from them.
next_gate: Search medical, embalming, laundry, perfumery and oil-production texts for local co-occurrence of textile + wetting/soaking + oil + squeeze/press, preferably in one sequential instruction.
